question: Should `tools.exec.denylist` override ordinary `security=full`/`ask=off` and durable trust while still permitting an explicitly authorized elevated-full invocation to bypass the STOP rule?
rationale: This defines a permanent execution-authorization boundary and compatibility contract; code review cannot decide whether elevated full is an intended break-glass escape from operator STOP rules.

options.title: Keep elevated break-glass
options.body: Accept the documented model where STOP rules force human approval for ordinary full/off execution but explicitly authorized elevated-full remains a bypass.

options.title: Make STOP rules absolute
options.body: Require denylist approval for elevated-full too and update the gateway, node, macOS, documentation, and regression contracts accordingly.

options.title: Narrow the policy surface
options.body: Pause this branch and redesign the feature around a smaller or separately enabled strict execution mode.

recommendation.title: Keep elevated break-glass
recommendation.body: Accept the documented model where STOP rules force human approval for ordinary full/off execution but explicitly authorized elevated-full remains a bypass.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing review discussion identifies steipete as the likely owner of the host exec security contract.
